findings: Fresh-context review of 0.2.10. Checked: package.json and package-lock.json both carry 0.2.10 and the same three bins (sl, simlocker, sl-mcp all pointing at bin/sl.js); the lockfile regenerated in a scratch copy with npm install --package-lock-only is byte for byte the same, so npm will not rewrite it; src/mcp.js and sl version say 0.2.10; npm test 29 pass with zero sl-drill folders under the system temp folder before and after the run; npm run lines 1131; no em dash in the diff. The README's Windows sentence holds by how npm writes its shims (a .cmd for cmd.exe, a .ps1 for PowerShell, a POSIX script for Git Bash) and by PowerShell resolving aliases before external commands, so sl is Set-Location there and simlocker is the name to use; this is reasoned from npm's behaviour, not run on Windows. One material finding was found and fixed in cf2034c: the comment added on line 450 of test/locker.test.js had swallowed the two asserts on a failed drill's exit code and restored commit; they are on their own line again and pass.
